Hi Tom / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery + next steps: 

- What we covered: production constraints (VPC + private deployment), target throughput (120 req/s peak), expected prompt lengths (avg ~512 tokens, peak ~2048), and SLO expectations (p50/p95/p99).
- Action items: I promised latency/throughput numbers from our recent runs that best match your workload and a short note on what configuration gave us those numbers. Attached: acme_benchmarks_q2.pdf and raw CSV output (redwood_latency.csv).

Key highlights from the attached:
- 512-token average: 35ms p50 / 78ms p95 / 124ms p99 (per-token generation, single-stream on T4-equivalent pool).
- 2048-token peak: ~1.6s p50 / 2.9s p95 / 4.1s p99 for single-request path (conventional GPT-style decoder); batching improves throughput but increases tail latency depending on your concurrency.
- Throughput note: on a 4-GPU Dedicated pool we measured ~180 warm tokens/sec aggregated for the model profile that maps closest to your evals (with KV caching enabled).

Neha (cc'd) will follow up with the exact 2048-token run details you asked about. From a process/next-steps perspective: if these numbers look in the right ballpark, we can schedule a short technical demo + a gated POC (2 week pilot) to validate on your real prompts.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm whether Acme wants the pilot in our hosted environment or in a Dedicated/Private deployment.
2) If Private, share a short list of compliance & network constraints so Neha can scope the deployment.
3) Pick a target week for a 30–45 min demo (we have availability next week).

Anything I missed? Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the attached.

Thanks,

Hi Tom — happy to expand on the test conditions. Quick notes below (pasted run results attached as acme_2048_p99_run.txt):

- 2048-token run: single-request path (no batching) on a warmed model instance (KV cache primed) — p50 1.6s / p95 2.9s / p99 4.1s. The run was performed with 8 concurrent worker processes hammering the pool to simulate a production ingress pattern; however the metric above is measured per-request latency, not aggregate.
- Batching: we ran a separate batched scenario with batch-size 4 that improved aggregate tokens/sec by ~35% but increased p99 by ~0.8s on average due to queuing. If Acme's priority is consistent sub-1s tail latency at 2048 tokens you'll want to prioritize dedicated low-latency instances and limit batching/queueing.
- Throughput: the ~180 warm tokens/sec number is aggregated across 4 GPUs under our Dedicated profile with KV caching; that assumed ~12 concurrent in-flight requests across the pool (conservative).

If helpful, we can spin up a short run using Acme prompts (securely uploaded) to replicate these numbers in your exact distribution. Also happy to include a small script to reproduce locally.

-Neha
